# Marks fixtures

**Origin**: `Marks.db3` (+ `-wal`/`-shm`) of a stock SAS.Planet install,
captured 2026-09-17.

**Backend confirmed**: this install uses the **SQLite (`Marks.db3`) backend**, not the legacy
`.sml` XML format — no `.sml` file exists anywhere on the live install or in the legacy repo's
`Test/` tree (searched both). So this fixture set only covers the SQLite/mORMot backend.

**How sliced**: copied the live `Marks.db3` + `Marks.db3-wal` + `Marks.db3-shm` to a scratch
location, ran `PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE);` there to fold the WAL into the main file (so the
fixture is a single self-contained `.db3`, no companion `-wal`/`-shm` needed), then copied the
result here. The legacy tree was never touched. `VACUUM` was attempted but fails under the stock
`sqlite3` CLI with `no such collation sequence: SYSTEMNOCASE` — the app registers a custom
`SYSTEMNOCASE` collation at runtime (via mORMot) that plain `sqlite3` doesn't have, so the file
was left un-vacuumed (124 KB, still tiny). **This is itself a finding**: any C++ reader/writer
for `Marks.db3` must register an ASCII case-insensitive collation named `SYSTEMNOCASE` before
opening the DB, or every text column (`uName`, `cName`, `mName`, `mDesc`, `miName`) will fail to
open/query correctly.

**Content**: this live install has never had any marks created — `Mark`, `Category`, `MarkImage`,
`MarkView`, `CategoryView`, `MarkAppearance`, `MarkMeta` are all empty (0 rows). Only `User` has
one row: `(ID=1, uName='sasgis')` — the default user created on first run. `MarkRTree_node` has 1
row (empty R-tree root node). This means the fixture exercises **schema and empty-state handling
only**, not actual mark geometry (WKB blobs, appearance/color codec, 80-bit Extended-float codec)
— no real mark data was available from either source. A real populated `Marks.db3` (or a minimal
`INSERT`, stated as synthetic) is still needed to test the marks-DB reader against actual
geometry.

**`Marks.db3.schema.sql`**: full `.schema` dump (all `CREATE TABLE`/`CREATE INDEX`/
`CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE` statements) taken from this fixture with `sqlite3 Marks.db3 ".schema"`.
Confirms: `Mark.mGeoWKB` is a BLOB (WKB geometry), full-text search via `MarkFTS` (fts4,
`tokenize=simple`), spatial index via `MarkRTree` (rtree module), and the `SYSTEMNOCASE`
collation used on every user-facing text column — this is the literal DDL needed since the
schema is not present verbatim in the legacy Pascal source.

**What it exercises**: marks-DB open/schema-validation, empty-database handling, default-user
bootstrap, and (via the schema dump) the exact column/type/collation/index contract the new C++
reader must replicate byte-for-byte.

## `SASPlanet.marks-sections.ini` (added 2026-10-12)

**Origin**: `SASPlanet.ini` (the same stock SAS.Planet install), sections `[MarkSystemConfig]`, `[MarkNewPoint]`,
`[MarkNewPoint_Name]`, `[MarkNewLine]`, `[MarkNewLine_Name]`, `[MarkNewPoly]`, `[MarkNewPoly_Name]`,
`[MarkNewCategory]`, `[PathToMarksIcons]` copied verbatim with `awk` (section header through the line before the next
header). CRLF line ends kept; the source file starts with a UTF-8 BOM, the extract does not (its first section is not
the first line of the source). Nothing edited by hand. **Exercises**: marks system config, mark templates, name
generators, category factory config read/write round trip.

## `system_nocase_vectors.tsv` (added 2026-10-12)

**Origin**: generated by `tools/gen_system_nocase_vectors.py` (formula-defined vectors). The script is a statement-by-statement Python transcription of the
Pascal source of the mORMot 2 library legacy links (checkout `2.4.17538`, head `b770705`, 2026-10-11; the legacy tree pins no revision):
`Utf8_SYSTEMNOCASE` (`db/mormot.db.raw.sqlite3.pas:6328-6341`), `Utf8ILComp` (`core/mormot.core.unicode.pas:7683-7798`), `UTF8_TABLE` (`:84-107`) and the
`WinAnsiToUp` table (`:12572-12581`, copied verbatim). It shares no code with the C++ port (`src/cg/marks/mormot/system_nocase.cpp`); two implementations
of one source agreeing is the proof available without a Windows run. Caveat: the Python generator is a second transcription of the same Pascal source by
the same author, so it catches slips, not a shared misreading of the source. Integer model: the 64-bit Windows build. An input for which the Pascal indexes
its table out of bounds makes the script raise, so no such vector exists (a legacy defect, reproduced). **Format**: `<hex of a>` TAB `<hex of b>` TAB
`<sign: -1|0|1>` TAB `<branch label>`; `-` is the empty string; `#` lines are comments. 928 vectors: empty strings, the ASCII path (case, punctuation
between `Z` and `a`, embedded NUL, prefixes), every code point U+0080…U+00FF against its table image / `Z` / `ß`, the U+00FF/U+0100 boundary, Cyrillic and
Greek (case-sensitive), 3- and 4-byte sequences, 5- and 6-byte lead bytes, overlong and unvalidated continuation bytes, invalid lead bytes and truncated
sequences on either side, equal prefixes of different length. **Regenerate**: `tools/gen_system_nocase_vectors.py` from the repository root (the test
checks the vector count). **Not yet proven** (needs a populated Windows file): the same order observed in an index page written by Windows SAS.Planet with
more than one row.
